Package game.crow

Class CrowSensing

java.lang.Object
game.crow.CrowSensing
public class CrowSensing extends Object
What a crow can sense from where it stands: food, other actors, and whether it is crowded. It answers the questions the crow's states ask when deciding what to do, so each state's transition logic stays a short, readable expression instead of repeating the same checks.

One instance describes one creature at one Location; the states are shared between crows, so they create a new one each time they need to sense. The creature passed in is always the one doing the sensing, so this class asks the creature for its own SensingRange. The AreaFactory is passed in by the state, as it is for CrowNavigation.

  • Constructor Details

    • CrowSensing

      public CrowSensing(Actor creature, Location here, AreaFactory areaFactory)
      Creates the senses of a creature at a Location. The creature's own sensing radius is asked for through its SensingRange capability, rather than this class assuming the creature is a Crow, so these senses could later be reused by another kind of stateful creature; a creature without one is simply assumed to have no sensing range at all.
      Parameters:
      creature - the creature doing the sensing
      here - the Location the creature senses from
      areaFactory - builds the Area of tiles within sensing range
